question: Reports on the work of committees of inquiry on the COVID-19 pandemic in Member States, such as Germany1, show that key decisions were prepared by confidential discussions during the COVID-19 pandemic. The Commission also worked with expert panels and national authorities on procurement and safeguards. 1.

Were representatives of the Commission or EU agencies (e.g. ECDC, EMA) involved in confidential meetings at Member State level, and does the Commission have any documents or minutes regarding such meetings?

What steps is the Commission taking to make the decision-making basis for EU pandemic policy fully accessible ex post, and will it fully disclose the relevant documents, minutes, opinions, communications and other documents at the request of the European Parliament or the public?
How does the Commission evaluate the results of Member States’ committees of inquiry to review its own policies and procurement strategies?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.11.2026) 1. From the reference supplied, it appears that the question refers to the ‘Review of the Coronavirus Pandemic and Lessons for Future Pandemic Events’ of the German federal parliament1. The Commission is not involved with the work of this national parliament’s commission and is not aware of its meetings. 2.

The main committee for EU coordination regarding health policy related to serious crossborder health threats is the Health Security Committee2. The minutes of its meetings as well as its opinions are published online3. 3. The responsibility for the definition of health policy and for the organisation and delivery of health services and medical care remains with the Member States.

It is their prerogative to review their national public health policy, inter alia through the setting up of inquiry committees or other bodies. The Commission is not involved with such national committees and does not therefore evaluate their results.

Pursuant to EU legislation4, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control carries out public health emergency preparedness assessments in all EU/European Economic Area (EEA) countries that assess the prevention, preparedness and response planning capacities of each5.

The Commission interacts with Member States on Joint Procurement of medical countermeasures as foreseen in the Joint Procurement Agreement6, whereas the decisions on joint procurement remain a national responsibility driven by national strategies. Procurement of medical countermeasures is also discussed with representatives of the Member States in the HERA (Health Emergency Preparedness and Response) Board7.
